title: Vanishing of H^0 of the product totalization of a complex of complexes whose p-th term has vanishing H^{-p}

standard_prerequisites.name: The differential on the product totalization Tot_pi of a double complex with entries A^{p,q} is, on elements of total degree n, the product over p + q = n of the components f^q_p + (-1)^p d^q_{A_p}
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the explicit form of the single equation d(x) = 0 for a cocycle representative x = (x_p) in the product, which is then unwound degree by degree.

standard_prerequisites.name: A class in H^0 is represented by a cocycle of total degree zero, i.e. by a family x = (x_p) in the product of the A^{p,-p} with d(x) = 0
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the shape of the object that has to be exhibited as a boundary, so that the goal becomes finding y with d(y) = x.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of a complex at a degree: if H^q(C) = 0 and an element z has d(z) = 0, then z is the boundary of some element of C^{q-1}
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 30116-30121, first with H^0(A_0) = 0 and then with H^{-1}(A_1) = 0
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the first element y_{-1} with d(y_{-1}) = x_0 and then the element y_{-2} that kills the corrected component x_1 + f_0(y_{-1}); the same step is iterated in the induction.

core_obligations: Recall that the differential on the product totalization is given on degree n elements by the product of the components f^q_p + (-1)^p d^q_{A_p}, and let xi be a class in H^0 represented by a cocycle x = (x_p) in the product of the A^{p,-p} (proof lines 30104-30114).
Unwind the equation d(x) = 0 in the lowest degree: this gives d_{A_0}(x_0) = 0, and since H^0(A_0) = 0 there is y_{-1} in A^{0,-1} with d_{A_0}(y_{-1}) = x_0 (proof lines 30115-30118).

Correct the next component: the equation d(x) = 0 together with the previous step gives d_{A_1}(x_1 + f_0(y_{-1})) = 0, and since H^{-1}(A_1) = 0 there is y_{-2} in A^{1,-2} with minus d_{A_1}(y_{-2}) equal to x_1 + f_0(y_{-1}) (proof lines 30119-30121).

Run the induction: for every p at least 0 find y_{-p-1} in A^{p,-p-1} satisfying (-1)^p d_{A_p}(y_{-p-1}) = x_p + f_{p-1}(y_{-p}), using the hypothesis H^{-p}(A_p) = 0 at the corresponding stage (proof lines 30122-30126).

Define y as the family (y_{-p-1}) and observe that d(y) = x, which exhibits the cocycle x as a boundary; since xi was an arbitrary class of H^0 of the totalization, the group H^0(Tot_pi) vanishes (proof lines 30127-30128).
proof_roadmap: Write down the differential of the product totalization on degree n elements and take a cocycle representative x = (x_p) of an arbitrary class in H^0 (proof lines 30104-30114).

Solve d(x) = 0 in the lowest degrees: H^0(A_0) = 0 produces y_{-1} with d(y_{-1}) = x_0, and H^{-1}(A_1) = 0 produces y_{-2} killing the corrected component x_1 + f_0(y_{-1}) (proof lines 30115-30121).

Iterate the same correction step to produce y_{-p-1} in A^{p,-p-1} with (-1)^p d(y_{-p-1}) = x_p + f_{p-1}(y_{-p}) for every p, using the hypothesis that H^{-p}(A_p) vanishes (proof lines 30122-30126).
Assemble the family y = (y_{-p-1}) and note that d(y) = x, so the class xi is zero and H^0 of the totalization vanishes (proof lines 30127-30128).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a complex of complexes of abelian groups A_0 -> A_1 -> A_2 -> ... whose p-th term has vanishing H^{-p}, forms the double complex A^{p,q} = A_p^q and concludes that the product totalization has vanishing H^0 (statement lines 30095-30102). The proof is an explicit degree-by-degree construction: after recalling the shape of the differential of the product totalization and taking a cocycle representative x = (x_p), the equation d(x) = 0 is unwound to give d(x_0) = 0, the vanishing of H^0(A_0) produces y_{-1} with x_0 = d(y_{-1}), and each further vanishing H^{-p}(A_p) = 0 produces the next element y_{-p-1} that kills the corrected component x_p + f_{p-1}(y_{-p}) (proof lines 30104-30126). What is not routine is tracking the two summands of the differential through the correction step, since the connecting maps f_p of the complex of complexes enter the equation for one component while the internal differentials act on the previous correction.
